$schema.description: Editor hint pointing at this schema. Ignored by the platform.

maturity.description: Marketplace maturity. stable modules sort before beta; beta modules show a Beta badge in the host marketplace.

sortOrder.description: Marketplace sort key within a maturity band (lower first). Defaults to 1000 when omitted.

requiresModuleSdk.description: Minimum version of the Portaki module SDK this module compiles against — the Rust crate portaki-sdk, published on crates.io. Renamed from requiresHostSdk, which did not say which SDK it meant: an npm @portaki/sdk also describes itself as the module SDK and carries an unrelated version line (3.2.1 against the crate 2.1.1).

sdkVersion.description: Version of the portaki-sdk crate the module was built against, as cargo resolved it. Written by portaki build, never by hand; portaki lint fails without it and refuses one older than the stable minimum (8.0.0) on the stable channel.

dispatchExamples.description: Ready-made calls the sandbox's Run tab offers, declared by example(label = …, input = …) on #[query] / #[command]. Written by portaki build.

title.description: What the button says — the example(label = …) text. Not named label: every label of a manifest must be a fr/en translation map.

permissions.description: Host operations this module is allowed to call. The manifest declares, the runtime enforces: any host op outside the granted set fails at execution. Omitted or empty means the module calls only the ambient ops, which need no permission — time.now, random.bytes, i18n.translate, log.

connectors.description: Connectors the build emitted (#[builtin_connector], #[custom_connector]), carried into the published manifest since portaki-sdk 9.3: the orchestrator lends a key only to a connector the published manifest declares, and the runtime pins each call to it (ADR-0021). Never hand-written.

queries.description: Read-only operations the module exports. Never hand-written: stamped from the build output at publish time, because only the build knows what the binary serves — a wasm module exports portaki_query and nothing else. The platform reads this to know which module to ask for a given operation, instead of dispatching blind and collecting wasm_handler_not_found from the ones that stay silent.

commands.description: Mutating operations the module exports. Same provenance as queries.

surfaces.description: Surfaces the binary exports (host / guest ids and their render symbols). Never hand-written: stamped from the build output, like queries.

entities.description: Typed-storage entities the module declares. Never hand-written: stamped from the build output, like queries.

hostSurfaces.description: Host dashboard surfaces. Types: property-workspace-tab (fullscreen listing tab), property-module-sheet (config cards / SDUI embedded in the module configure sheet), property-stats-card (typed stats tile served by the statsSummary query with key = pathSegment; label and icon name the tile), property-stats-detail (host SDUI surface whose id is pathSegment, rendered with input.periodDays; same pathSegment as its tile), workspace-timeline-task (dated tasks served by the timelineTasks query), stay-detail (SDUI embed on stay detail with stayId input), stay-action (stay detail button that opens a modal hosting module SDUI), property-listing-card (a card of the listing's « Fiche & coordonnées » settings page: the shell draws the card frame and title, the module fills it, and its draft publishes with the listing's own Publier).

guestSurfaces.description: Guest booklet URL routes beyond the implicit home.card (path may include :params).

emails.description: Module-owned timed / transactional emails. When command is set, the platform may dispatch that Wasm command (module owns gate + host::email::send). catchUpOnPropertyPublish redispatches after draft publish; catchUpOnConfigUpdate after host updateConfig (promotes module KV then redispatches); dispatchOnStayCreated on stay create. Delivery dedup uses id per stay.

emailVars.description: Variables the module gives Portaki guest emails, per template, declared by #[portaki_sdk::email_vars] (portaki build writes it). The platform calls the module's emailContext query for a declared template and merges the declared keys into that email; nothing else the module answers is read. Each variable is rendered only by some templates (portaki_sdk::email::EmailVar::templates).

emailBlocks.description: Kinds of block the module adds to Portaki stay emails, per email, declared by #[portaki_sdk::email_blocks] (portaki build writes it). The platform calls the module's emailContext query for a declared email and reads the `blocks` key of the answer. Exclusive with emailVars: a module gives an email variables or blocks, never both. Each kind is rendered only by some emails (portaki_sdk::email::BlockType::templates).

core.description: A core module of the booklet: installed on every property, always active, with no on/off switch, and absent from the modules list and the marketplace. Declared by portaki_module!(core); a core module must declare at least one host or guest surface.

audience.description: Who the module works for. host modules (e.g. calendar import) are never shown to guests and cannot be placed on the booklet board. Any other value is read as guest.

feeds.description: Modules this one supplies from behind the scenes, when it has no guest surface of its own (e.g. a lock that hands its keypad code to access-guide). The catalogue reads it as: <name> provides <what> to the <module> module.

what.description: What it supplies, as a noun phrase: { "fr": "le code clavier", "en": "the keypad code" }.

errors.description: The refusal codes the module may raise (portaki_module!(error = "…"), raised with refuse!). A module's error text never reaches the host, since free text could carry guest data out: the platform shows a refusal only when its code is listed here, with the label of the i18n key errors.<code>. On the wire a refusal reads module_refused:<code>.

changelog.description: What is new in this version, shown to hosts who have an older one installed: two or three short lines, one entry per line with every language side by side ({ "fr": "…", "en": "…" }). Filled by portaki release from --notes (fr:… per language), or else from this version's section of CHANGELOG.<lang>.md (CHANGELOG.md for the default language); omitted when nothing says anything. A stable version stays pending at the registry until it has a line in every language of the module's listing.

capabilities.description: Capabilities the module provides to its peers, stamped from the build output by `portaki build` (#[portaki_sdk::capability(provided, …)]) — never hand-written. The platform finds peers with them: host::module::list_by_capability.

provided.description: A capability id alone, or { id, shares, path, commands } when the module shares some of its own settings, names the guest path consumers open, or lets them call some of its commands.

shares.description: Keys of this module's own config.fields that consumers read, read-only, as ModulePeer.shared. Only the published values are shared — never the draft — and never a secret: a secret field or a structured list with item.secret sub-keys is refused by the conformance battery and dropped again by the platform.

path.description: One of this module's own guestSurfaces paths, without :params: where a consumer opens this capability (ModulePeer.path, then Action::navigate).

commands.description: This module's own commands a module that depends on this capability (capabilities.depends) may call. Absent: no peer command at all — the capability is reached by navigation only.

depends.description: Capabilities named by modules (not the platform) that this module relies on: #[portaki_sdk::capability(required|optional, id = "…")]. The platform resolves providers among the property's installed modules, and accepts a peer command only from a module that depends on the capability.

optional.description: The module works without a provider. Absent = false.

resources.description: Unstable (SDK 11 proof): the resources the SDK stores for the module (#[collection]). Fields have the shape of config.fields.

config.description: Host configuration, declared by #[portaki_sdk::config] (portaki build writes it). The platform validates and stores what the host saves (updateConfig), encrypts secret fields at rest and passes the result to the module as context.moduleConfig. A required field left empty flags the install requiresConfig / incomplete and blocks publication; a recommended one only warns. Empty = absent, null, blank string, empty list or object; toggle and number are never empty. The dashboard also reads globalAlert and defaults.

hostScheduledSync.description: Host-side sync the platform runs on a schedule (and on demand), without business logic in the API. With platformFetch, the platform calls sourcesQuery to list what to fetch, downloads it, then hands the payloads to applyQuery; both are then required. Without it, the platform runs the module host action hostAction, then stayImportQuery if set to import the resulting stays.

hostAction.description: Host action the platform runs when platformFetch is false. A host action with this name is treated as the scheduled sync.

stayImportQuery.description: Query read after hostAction to import stays, when platformFetch is false.

platformFetch.description: The platform fetches the sources, not the module.

sourcesQuery.description: Query listing the sources to fetch, when platformFetch is true.

applyQuery.description: Query receiving the fetched payloads, when platformFetch is true.

format.description: localized: the host formats it (TipTap document or Markdown).

accept.description: file: the media types taken (<input accept>).

maxItems.description: structured: at most this many rows.

item.description: structured: the fields of each row, merged by id.

type.description: secret values are encrypted at rest and masked when read back; readonly fields are never required. structured is an object or a list (contacts, bins, opening hours…) edited by the module's own host surface, never rendered by a generic form. localized is a text per language, stored as an i18nStringMap ({"fr": "…", "en": "…"}, short codes): a string saved from the host form is written into the host's language, the other languages are kept; empty when no language has a non-blank text.

local.description: Depends on where the property is (a position, a distance, an address, local hours, a parking spot): a copy from another property lands in the draft marked « À vérifier » for this key, until the host edits or confirms it. Absent = false.

visibleWhen.description: otherField=value: the field is shown — in the host form and to the guest — only while that other field holds exactly this value (serialized; a toggle is true or false). The platform reads a hidden field as absent from the guest's booklet (the guest assistant never sees it).

reveal.description: On a secret field, or on a structured list whose rows hold secret sub-keys (item.secret — then it covers each of them, keyed <key>[].<sub>): where the module shows the value, closed. guest_pre_arrival — the guest booklet before the stay; guest_stay — the guest booklet during the stay (never after departure); arrival_email — the emailContext answer the platform puts in arrival e-mails. Anywhere else (host surfaces, logs, events, e-mails the module sends, other answers) the conformance battery fails the version. A reveal added since the previous stable is justified in the release notes like an added permission (permissionReasons key reveal:<key>:<place>).

item.description: The rows of a structured list (or the keys of a structured object). A save merges each received row into the stored one — same id, else same position: sub-keys it does not carry are kept, localized sub-keys follow the localized rule.

id.description: Sub-key identifying a row. Absent: rows are matched by position.

localized.description: Sub-keys holding a text per language (i18nStringMap).

secret.description: Sub-keys encrypted at rest, like a secret field: a save that leaves one out, empty or masked keeps the stored value (row matched by id, else position); null clears it.

fields.description: The row's fields, from its #[params] shape, stamped by portaki build: what a tool building or checking rows (the listing import) holds them to. Absent when the row type declares no shape.

type.description: string, boolean, integer, number, array, map, json or ref.

ref.description: The type a ref names, e.g. I18nText.

format.description: uuid, date-time, date or time, on a string.

items.description: The element of an array, same shape as the #[params] field type (type, ref, format, items…).

required.description: False for an Option or a #[serde(default)] field.

operation.description: An operation the module exports, stamped from the build output by `portaki build` — never hand-written. Same shape as portaki_sdk::manifest::ManifestQuery and ManifestCommand.

name.description: The name the platform dispatches, e.g. mapMarkers.

fn.description: The Rust function serving it, e.g. map_markers.

args.description: The argument type name, when the handler takes one.

params.description: The argument fields, when that type carries #[portaki_sdk::params]. Descriptive only: the platform never validates a dispatch against it.

guest.description: Guest-only when true — the `guest` flag on #[query] / #[command]: the platform refuses a host call to it (operation_not_host_callable). Host-only when false: the platform refuses a guest call (operation_not_guest_callable). Always written by portaki build; its absence marks a manifest stamped by an older SDK.

permission.description: kv — kv.get/set/delete/list, the module's own key-value namespace. repo — repo.find/create/delete over the module's own isolated schema; implies module-owned tables, reserved to official modules during beta. email — email.send, which reaches real guests. events — events.emit, which publishes to the platform outbox. platform — capabilities.has, module.status, module.listByCapability. stay:guest_contact:read — the guest's email and phone on the invocation stay context; the rest of the stay (dates, channel, party size, announced arrival, guest language) needs no permission. Not needed to email the guest: email.send with the guest audience lets the platform resolve the address. guest:files — the guest may attach an image (ImageUpload field) to this module's commands; the platform stores it and refuses the upload to a module without this permission. host:files — files.read, the bytes of a file the host attached to this module (a GPX track); only a file of this property and this module is served. connectors:<id> — connector.call restricted to that connector (e.g. connectors:nuki); the credential resolver refuses any connector not listed here.

type.description: Where the dashboard mounts the surface — see hostSurfaces.

pathSegment.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 64 at most: the fronts build API and dashboard URLs from it. For property-workspace-tab: URL segment under /listings/[id]/. For property-module-sheet: stable id (usually the module id). For property-stats-card: the key passed to statsSummary. For property-stats-detail: the id of the host surface rendering the detail, equal to the pathSegment of its tile. For property-listing-card: stable id (usually the module id).

id.description: Stable delivery id (dedup key with module + stay)

command.description: Wasm command to dispatch (e.g. sendFormAvailable); module owns gate + email body

catchUpOnPropertyPublish.description: When true, platform redispatches command for upcoming/active property stays after draft publish

catchUpOnConfigUpdate.description: When true, after host updateConfig the platform promotes module KV draft then redispatches for upcoming/active property stays (Save without property Publish)

dispatchOnStayCreated.description: When true, platform dispatches command on StayCreated

surfaceId.description: Wasm/guest surface id (e.g. explore.detail, explore.item): lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, 64 at most — it ends up in API URLs.

path.description: Guest URL path under /p/[accessKey]/ (e.g. appliances, appliances/:deviceId): segments of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, or :params.

labelKey.description: i18n key for booklet nav label (e.g. nav.appliances)

role.description: card (default booklet card) | arrival-formality (composed into Accueil formalities; may embed HostFragment for regulatory.police-form) | post-stay (rendered on the dedicated end-of-stay screen once the stay is over) | upcoming (compact prep card rendered on the pre-arrival timeline before check-in) | status-cell (the access cell of the booklet status strip, on the module's own reveal schedule) | status-note (the pull quote under the status strip: the host's word)

embedsHostFragments.description: Host fragment ids this surface composes (e.g. regulatory.police-form). Shells skip standalone host UI for those fragments when such a surface is enabled.
